chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskān, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyād, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

She inherits and is inherited from as long as she has the right of return (raj'ah) from the first two divorces, until she performs the ritual bath. The solution regarding these two reports is what we have previously presented, by interpreting them as being based on precaution (taqiyyah). Our Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) reconciled these reports by saying: If he divorces her at the end of her purity period, she observes the waiting period by counting her menstrual cycles; and if he divorces her at the beginning of it, she observes the waiting period by counting the purity periods (which are the clean days). This is a close (plausible) solution, except that the first one is what we have previously presented.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Precautionary dissimulation, a concept in Shia Islam where one conceals their true beliefs or rulings to avoid harm.
key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: The right of return, referring to a revocable divorce where the husband can take back his wife during the waiting period without a new contract.
key_terms.الطَّلِيقَتَيْنِ الْأُولَتَيْنِ: The first two divorces, which are revocable (raj'ah) as opposed to the third which is irrevocable.
key_terms.الْأَطْهَارُ: The clean days, referring to the periods of purity in a woman's cycle.
key_terms.الْأَقْرَاءِ: Purity periods (days between menstruations), used as an alternative method to calculate the waiting period.
key_terms.الْحِيَضِ: Menstrual cycles, used here to calculate the waiting period (iddah).
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلَ: She performs the ritual bath (ghusl), which marks the end of the waiting period for a divorced woman.

ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period (Iddah) calculated for a woman with a revocable divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the status of a woman in her 'iddah following one of the first two revocable divorces, noting that mutual inheritance persists until the completion of the waiting period. Shaykh al-Tusi reconciles apparent contradictions in the reports by attributing them to taqiyyah and proposing a juristic distinction: if divorced at the end of purity, the 'iddah is counted by menstruation, whereas if divorced at the beginning, it is counted by purity days. This reflects the Shia scholarly method of harmonizing conflicting hadiths through contextual interpretation and practical legal application.
